stops.note: 'holy one, saint'; the feast of All Saints on 1 November was known as All Hallows, and in 835 Louis the Pious, at Pope Gregory IV's urging, made it a holy day across the Frankish empire
contracted from All-Hallow-Even; Robert Burns's poem 'Halloween' (1785) records Ayrshire fortune-telling customs on the night, which drew on the Gaelic festival of Samhain
Irish and Scottish immigrants carried the customs to the US, where trick-or-treating spread in the 1930s-50s

current_meaning: the night of 31 October, celebrated with costumes and trick-or-treating
